title: Doppler Effect (moving source/observer/wall, angled motion)
theory:
With sound speed $V$, source speed $v_s$ and observer speed $v_o$ **along the line of sight**:
$$f' = f\,\frac{V \pm v_o}{V \mp v_s} \qquad \text{(upper signs for approach)}$$
Mnemonic: **observer motion edits the numerator** (how fast wavefronts are met); **source motion edits the denominator** (the wavelength itself is changed). A reflecting **wall is a two-step device**: it first *hears* as an observer, then *re-emits* that frequency as a source. Only the **radial** velocity component shifts pitch — resolve angled motion first.

formulas.description: wall moving toward source+observer (receive as observer, re-emit as source)

framework: Apply the formula leg by leg (source→wall, wall→listener).
For beats, subtract the two received frequencies.

problems.title: Speaker between a wall and a listener (parts 1–5)

parts.title: Direct sound at A (source approaching)
parts.parameters:
- Given (left→right): wall D with rider C on its front face — B, a speaker of frequency $f$ — A, an observer; sound speed $V$. Parts (1)–(3): B moves **right** at $v$ (toward A, away from D); everything else static. Parts (4)–(5): B and A static; D and C move **right** at $v$ (toward B).
- Find: direct frequency at A; wall-reflected frequency at A; beat rate at A; frequency heard at C; reflected frequency at A with the wall moving.

parts.title: Wall-reflected sound at A (source receding from the wall)
parts.parameters:
- Given (left→right): wall D with rider C on its front face — B, a speaker of frequency $f$ — A, an observer; sound speed $V$. Parts (1)–(3): B moves **right** at $v$ (toward A, away from D); everything else static. Parts (4)–(5): B and A static; D and C move **right** at $v$ (toward B).
- Find: direct frequency at A; wall-reflected frequency at A; beat rate at A; frequency heard at C; reflected frequency at A with the wall moving.
parts.formulas: static wall receives $f\frac{V}{V+v}$ and re-emits it unchanged; A is static.

parts.title: Beat frequency at A
parts.parameters:
- Given (left→right): wall D with rider C on its front face — B, a speaker of frequency $f$ — A, an observer; sound speed $V$. Parts (1)–(3): B moves **right** at $v$ (toward A, away from D); everything else static. Parts (4)–(5): B and A static; D and C move **right** at $v$ (toward B).
- Find: direct frequency at A; wall-reflected frequency at A; beat rate at A; frequency heard at C; reflected frequency at A with the wall moving.
parts.conclusion: for $v \ll V$ this is $\approx 2fv/V$ — the standard first-order beat estimate (see Topic 31).

parts.title: Frequency at C (observer approaching a static source)
parts.parameters:
- Given (left→right): wall D with rider C on its front face — B, a speaker of frequency $f$ — A, an observer; sound speed $V$. Parts (1)–(3): B moves **right** at $v$ (toward A, away from D); everything else static. Parts (4)–(5): B and A static; D and C move **right** at $v$ (toward B).
- Find: direct frequency at A; wall-reflected frequency at A; beat rate at A; frequency heard at C; reflected frequency at A with the wall moving.

parts.title: Reflected frequency at A with the wall moving toward B
parts.parameters:
- Given (left→right): wall D with rider C on its front face — B, a speaker of frequency $f$ — A, an observer; sound speed $V$. Parts (1)–(3): B moves **right** at $v$ (toward A, away from D); everything else static. Parts (4)–(5): B and A static; D and C move **right** at $v$ (toward B).
- Find: direct frequency at A; wall-reflected frequency at A; beat rate at A; frequency heard at C; reflected frequency at A with the wall moving.
parts.formulas: wall as observer (approaching): receives $f\frac{V+v}{V}$; wall as source (approaching A): multiply by $\frac{V}{V-v}$.
parts.conclusion: the $V$'s always cancel in the wall composition — a moving-mirror reflection is **always** $\frac{V+v}{V-v}$ on approach. Sanity sweep: every "toward" configuration must *raise* the pitch; all five answers comply.

parts.parameters:
- Given: source frequency $f = 660$ Hz; sound speed $V = 330$ m/s; observer walks at 5 m/s along the ground, directly away from the point O below the source; the source S sits 9 m horizontally and 12 m vertically from the observer's position.
- Find: observed frequency, 2 significant figures.
parts.formulas: distance SO via right triangle; radial speed = (speed) × (horizontal leg / hypotenuse); $f' = f\dfrac{V - v_r}{V}$ (receding observer).
parts.conclusion: only the **line-of-sight component** (3 m/s) shifts the pitch — plugging the full 5 m/s gives 650 Hz, option (a), the planted trap. Spot 9-12-15 instantly, and note $660/330 = 2$ turns the whole computation into one multiplication.
